facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" was authored by Robert Louis Stevenson.
The eBook was released on June 27, 2008.
The eBook can be accessed online at www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/43.
The text is credited to David Widger.
Mr. Utterson is a reserved and austere lawyer.
Mr. Hyde trampled a young girl during a Sunday walk.
Hyde paid the girl's family a hundred pounds using a cheque.
Utterson and Enfield agreed to avoid discussing Hyde further.
Mr. Utterson examined Dr. Jekyll's will after dinner.
Dr. Jekyll's will bequeathed all his possessions to Edward Hyde.
Utterson sought out Dr. Lanyon to discuss his concerns about Hyde.
Utterson learned that Hyde had access to Dr. Jekyll's home.
Dr. Jekyll hosted a dinner for a few close friends, including Mr. Utterson.
Utterson expressed concerns about Jekyll's connection to Mr. Hyde.
Jekyll urged Utterson to promise to look after Hyde's interests after his departure.
Utterson agreed to Jekyll's request to ensure justice for Hyde.
Sir Danvers Carew was murdered by Mr. Hyde in October of 18—.
A maid witnessed Hyde attack Carew with a heavy cane.
Mr. Utterson identified the broken cane as one he had given to Dr. Henry Jekyll.
Hyde's living quarters were found to be luxurious yet ransacked.
Mr. Utterson visits Dr. Jekyll in the late afternoon.
Dr. Jekyll is shaken by news of a murder involving Sir Danvers Carew.
Utterson discusses a letter from Edward Hyde with his clerk, Mr. Guest.
Mr. Guest notes similarities in handwriting between Hyde's letter and a note from Jekyll.
Mr. Hyde vanished after the murder of Sir Danvers.
Dr. Jekyll appeared revitalized for over two months after Hyde's disappearance.
Dr. Lanyon was gravely ill and refused to discuss Jekyll.
Lanyon left Utterson a sealed letter to be opened only after Jekyll's death or disappearance.
Mr. Utterson and Mr. Enfield stop in front of a door associated with Mr. Hyde.
Dr. Jekyll is found sitting by an open window.
Jekyll declines to join Utterson and Enfield outside.
Utterson murmurs a plea for forgiveness as they leave.
Mr. Utterson is visited by Poole, Dr. Jekyll's butler.
Utterson discovers Hyde's lifeless body in Jekyll's cabinet.
A will is found naming Utterson as the beneficiary.
Utterson plans to return with the police to investigate.
Dr. Lanyon received a registered letter from Dr. Henry Jekyll on January 9th.
Jekyll asked Lanyon to retrieve a specific drawer from his cabinet.
Lanyon broke into Jekyll's cabinet with the help of a locksmith.
The mysterious man who arrived at midnight transformed into Jekyll.
Dr. Henry Jekyll creates a potion that separates his two identities.
Jekyll initially feels exhilarated by Edward Hyde's reckless behavior.
Jekyll commits a violent crime that prompts a moral crisis.
Jekyll ultimately succumbs to temptation and loses control to Hyde.
